remaining_uncertainties: Forward citation lists were only partially retrievable: Semantic Scholar citations succeeded for five seeds (KYC 28 citing works, 2512.02902 17, LIBERO-RIG 1, CMA 1, RSB 1) after repeated retries, but More Structure (2607.09825) and 2610.01626 stayed at HTTP 429, and OpenAlex filter=cites remained rate-limited. No citing work found in the five retrieved sets tests whether failure-mode composition predicts representation benefit, but the two missing seeds leave that possibility open.

The surviving candidate C1 was narrowed after a second full-text pass: LIBERO-RIG already defines 'tolerance per axis' (Table 5) and More Structure already demonstrates the mechanism (spatial grounding fixes Near-Miss 31%->2.5% but leaves No-Grasp unchanged). What remains untested is only the cross-task predictive relation, and no pilot evidence exists that same-task/different-failure-mode variants can be constructed.
41 of 94 registered papers were read at abstract level only (arXiv HTML rate limits); they may contain direct competitors that would change the crowding judgement.
Conference-versus-arXiv version differences were not compared for most entries.
Real-robot evidence in this literature rests on 20-30 trials per condition, which limits the statistical strength of any action-level claim, including future ones.
Whether a measurement/prediction contribution is acceptable as the master's small paper is an advisor judgement that literature research cannot settle.
conclusion: After 130 queries and 94 registered papers, three passes and partial forward-citation chasing, five of seven directions fail the hard vetoes. The citation audit strengthened this: KYC's 28 citing works are all viewpoint-robustness variants, and new finds (CAG/LIBERO-CF, paired instruction dependence) further crowd the evidence-use direction. One direction survives only in a narrowed, medium-low-confidence form: whether baseline failure-mode composition plus the intervention's reduction of the operative spatial error predicts the action benefit of a spatial upgrade. Its mechanism is already demonstrated on a single task and per-axis tolerance is already operationalised, so the remaining contribution is a cross-task prediction study whose utility must be shown as selection value, not correlation. The report recommends no experiment until seven explicit gates are met, and states that if the predictive relation does not hold, no candidate in this scope qualifies.
